# Fetching Smash Sources

How to get the full text from each common source. Add to this file whenever a new source trick is learned.

## SmashWiki (ssbwiki.com)

- **Fetch raw wikitext, not the rendered page:**
  `curl -sL "https://www.ssbwiki.com/index.php?title=<Page_Name>&action=raw"`
  The raw text keeps game-scope templates that summarizing fetchers lose.
- **Game templates in wikitext:** `{{SSBU|X}}` is Ultimate, `{{SSB4|X}}` is Smash 4, `{{SSBB|X}}` is Brawl,
  `{{SSBM|X}}` is Melee, `{{SSB|X}}` is 64.
- **Page layout:** series-wide pages usually have general sections followed by `===Specifics in ''<Game>''===`
  subsections. Read the Ultimate subsection first, then check the general text against it.
- **Character pages:** `<Character>_(SSBU)` is the Ultimate page. Move subpages look like
  `<Character>_(SSBU)/<Move>`.
- **`<ref>` tags** point to the original evidence (datamine tweets, videos). Copy them into the page's Sources
  dropdown and `% research:` lines (docs-writing standard).

## Frame data

- **SmashDb** (`pkgs/ds/data/*.parquet`, queried with `ds.ai.smashdb`) is the in-repo source of truth. Check it
  before going to the web.
- **ultimateframedata.com** is a good second source for cross-checking.

## Twitter / X, Discord

- X usually needs a login, so WebFetch fails. Ask the user to paste the tweet text, or use a mirror if one is
  available.
- Discord: use content the user pastes or exports from channels they're in. Don't run self-bots or scrape
  servers, since both violate Discord's ToS. Record channel name, author and date for provenance.

## YouTube

- Use the video title and description as leads. When exact wording matters, ask the user for timestamps or a
  transcript.
